data.title: Director Service Accounts (m/f/d)
data.description:
Director Service Accounts @ Sereact 🦾

Director Service Accounts (m/f/d) · Stuttgart, with frequent travel to customer sites across Europe · Reports to the VP Operations · Full-time

Who we are

Sereact builds the robot brain for physical work. Cortex, our vision-language-action foundation model, is hardware-agnostic: the same model runs single-arm and dual-arm systems and mobile manipulators that pick, sort and handle returns in live production across Europe and the US. Customers include Zalando, IKEA, BMW, Rohlik and DHL.

Founded in 2021 in Stuttgart, with an R&D hub in Zurich and a US office in Boston. We have raised more than $145 million, most recently a Series B led by Headline, with Zalando as a strategic investor. We work in small, senior teams with a flat structure; execution counts more than titles.

Why this role, why now

The Site Acceptance Test is where a deployment ends and a customer’s operation begins. From that day our robots pick in someone else’s building, every shift, against targets the customer measures. Many of our customers buy Sereact as a service: they pay for robots that work, not for robots that were delivered.

Our deployments are growing from single robots to fleets, and the site that performs is the site that grows. We now want one leader who owns every live site from SAT on: keeps it at target, brings it everything we ship in software and hardware, speaks for the customer inside Sereact, and turns a working site into a growing one.

The Real-World Learning Loop runs through your sites

Cortex learns from live deployments. Every station at a customer is part of that loop, so a station that is down is more than a service problem: a cell sitting dark is a stopped sensor.

  • In-Situ Policy Execution. Every live station runs the current policy in a real operation. Your surface on it: each site at target, every shift.

  • Continuous Data Acquisition. Robots annotate their own work while they run. Your surface on it: stations that run and stay connected, so the data keeps coming.

  • Data Curation and Learning. Failures and edge cases decide what Cortex learns next. Your surface on it: what your sites tell us reaches engineering and research with the context they need.

  • Evaluation and Policy Redeployment. Updated policies pass validation gates before they return to the fleet. Your surface on it: they land in your customers’ operations on a schedule the customer can plan around, with a way back if something is off.

A site that runs well teaches Cortex more, and it grows.

Responsibilities

  • Take over every site at SAT. Set the standard for what a site needs before your team takes it on: documentation, open points, spare parts, contacts and targets. If a site is not ready, it stays with deployment until it is.

  • Keep every site at target. Own each site’s performance against its contract: availability, throughput and pick success. See a problem coming before the customer does, and run the recovery plan when a site falls behind.

  • Run planned change. Software releases and model updates reach customer operations in a rhythm customers can plan around: release notes, change windows, blackout periods, validation on site and a rollback path.

  • Run hardware updates and retrofits across the installed base, from new gripper generations to station upgrades and fixes, with Hardware Engineering and the field teams, without stopping the customer’s operation.

  • Get every site ready for peak: hypercare and coverage plans for the weeks that matter most to our customers, from Black Friday to the January returns wave.

  • Be the customer’s advocate inside Sereact. Bring their priorities into product, R&D, hardware and operations, make sure what we promised at SAT holds, and own the customer communication when something goes wrong.

  • Take each site from SAT to expansion with Strategic Accounts: the performance evidence, the site capacity and the technical plan for the next stations. Strategic Accounts own the contract; you make the expansion ready to happen.

  • Report site health customers trust: one view of every site, monthly performance reports and the operational part of every business review.

  • Build and lead the Service Accounts team: Service Account Managers who each own a portfolio of live sites, and a playbook that still works when the installed base is ten times larger.

  • Work hand in hand with Deployment, Technical Support & Field Service, Hardware Engineering, R&D and Strategic Accounts, so a live site gets one coordinated answer, not five.

Not in scope, by design

  • Deployment up to SAT stays with our deployment teams. You set the bar for what you take over.

  • Incidents, the support desk, field technicians and spare parts logistics stay with Technical Support & Field Service. You own the site; they own the ticket.

  • Contracts, pricing and the expansion deal itself stay with Strategic Accounts. You make the case; they sign it.

  • Product and hardware design stay with engineering. You bring them what the field needs.

What makes this role hard

  • Every change to a live operation is a risk, and not changing is a risk too: the fleet only gets better if updates reach it. You make both safe.

  • Our robots work in other people’s buildings: their WMS, their conveyors, their shift patterns, their peak. Much of what decides a site’s performance is not ours, and it is still your problem.

  • You sit between the customer and our teams. Sometimes the customer’s priority is not ours. You argue for it, or you explain honestly why not.

  • The installed base grows faster than any team. What works by heroics today breaks at ten times the size.

Your first 12 months

  • First 90 days: know every live site and its people; one named owner, one health view and a clear status against target for each; a handover standard at SAT agreed with deployment.

  • By month 6: releases and retrofits in a rhythm customers can plan around; peak season run on hypercare plans; account plans with Strategic Accounts for the largest customers; the first Service Account Managers hired.

  • By month 12: every site at target or on a dated recovery plan; expansions coming out of the installed base; a playbook ready to take to the US.

What you bring

  • 8+ years owning live installations of complex automation after go-live (warehouse automation, intralogistics, robotics or comparable 24/7 systems), as service account manager, technical account manager, customer success or service delivery lead, including at least three years leading a team.

  • You did it while the installed base grew from tens to hundreds of sites, and you built the processes rather than inheriting them.

  • Technical enough to read a log, follow a root cause and hold your own with engineers. Commercial enough to sit with a customer’s operations director and talk performance, cost and growth.

  • You have run releases, upgrades and retrofit programs in live operations without stopping them.

  • Customers trust you because you tell them early and you tell them straight.

  • Fluent English and German; another European language is a plus.

  • You are happy to spend a large part of your week at customer sites.

Nice to have: subscription or Robotics-as-a-Service models · goods-to-person and AS/RS integrations · e-commerce, returns or grocery fulfilment · experience in both a scale-up and an established automation vendor.

Not the right fit: account management without technical depth, or running a ticket queue without ever owning a customer.

Three questions we will ask you

  1. Tell us about a live site that fell behind its targets. What did you change in the first two weeks, and how did it end?

  2. A customer’s peak starts in four weeks. Engineering wants to ship a model update and a gripper retrofit before then. What do you do?

  3. How do you know a site is about to grow, or about to leave, before the customer tells you?

What we offer

  • A fleet in live production that grows every month, and the mandate to build the team that keeps it at target.

  • A key role in the operations leadership of a company scaling from Europe into the US, with equity.

  • Travel, accommodation and meals covered when you are on site.

  • Our HQ in Stuttgart, with teams in Zurich and Boston.

How we hire

Conversations with our VP Operations and the founders, a working session on a real case from one of our live sites, and time with the team in Stuttgart. We move fast.

data.title: Head of Product | Intch
data.description:
About Intch

Intch is a professional social network with a marketplace for part-time work. You can think of it as a professional network built for senior specialists who take on meaningful contracts alongside their main work. A typical contract lasts from three to six months. The product is used in 140 countries and is available in up to 20 languages. Intch has fewer than 40 people and four product areas, with three already live and one preparing to launch. Intch is rethinking how people and companies find each other and build trust online.

What you’ll do

  • Own the B2C product end to end, including its P&L.

  • Set the product direction and own the 3–6 month roadmap across strategy, experimentation, and delivery.

  • Drive growth through hypothesis-driven experiments and measurable improvements in acquisition, activation, and retention.

  • Own the product metrics and use data to guide decisions and prioritisation.

  • Conduct CustDev interviews and build a deep understanding of user behaviour across a global, multilingual audience.

  • Partner with the B2B product teams to make the B2C product the connective layer across Intch’s product ecosystem.

  • Report directly to the founder and CEO and take over the product vertical they currently lead. There is no CPO at Intch: all product owners report to the CEO, so this is the most senior product position in the company.

What you need to succeed

  • 5+ years of experience in product management.

  • A strong B2C growth track record, including experiments, acquisition, and measurable results.

  • Proven experience scaling a product that already has strong product–market fit.

  • A strong record of improving key metrics such as growth, activation, and retention.

  • Strong product sense and a hypothesis-driven approach to problem-solving.

  • Comfort working with data and translating insights into action.

  • Experience working in a startup or another fast-moving, high-ownership environment.

  • High autonomy, accountability, and comfort working without micromanagement.

  • Fluent Russian.

What you get

  • Full ownership of a profitable, fast-growing product and its P&L, reporting directly to the founder.

  • A deliberately compact team (under 40 people) where everyone has a large area of ownership and streamlined collaboration.

  • Metrics-driven culture: every function, including support and payments, owns numbers. Your P&L is your scoreboard.

  • Flat, cross-pollinating structure: anyone in the company can bring a validated idea to your product. You can do the same across other verticals.

  • Paid vacation and sick leave.

data.title: (Senior) Customer Success Manager:in SaaS Energiewirtschaft (w/m/d) - Remote
data.description:
Was Dich erwartet

Als Teil unseres Customer Success Teams stehst Du in direktem Kontakt mit unseren Kunden und Software-Nutzern aus dem Bereich der kaufmännischen Betriebsführung von Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen. Du begleitest eigenständig neue Kunden durch einen strukturieren Einrichtungsprozess der Software opti.node und stellst so sicher, dass sie den größtmöglichen Nutzen aus der Anwendung ziehen können. Die Anforderungen unserer Kunden sind oftmals anspruchsvoll und nicht selten innovativ - in diesen Fällen bist du nicht auf dich alleine gestellt, sondern hast hoch qualifizierte Kolleg:innen aus allen Bereichen, mit denen offene Fragen und neue Herausforderungen besprochen und gelöst werden können.

node.energy ermöglicht mit klugen Software-as-a-Service-Lösungen professionellen Betreibern von Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen neue Geschäftsmodelle ganz einfach umzusetzen und damit profitabel zu bleiben. Hierfür führt opti.node alle Daten für die kaufmännische Betriebsführung von Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen zusammen und automatisiert anspruchsvolle Verwaltungsaufgaben und energiewirtschaftliche Geschäftsprozesse. Bereits heute vertrauen Betreiber von mehr als 14.000 Windkraft- und PV-Anlagen, die mehr als ein Drittel des deutschen Grünstroms erzeugen, auf opti.node.

Wir suchen dich als (Senior) Customer Success Manager:in (w/m/d) in Voll- oder Teilzeit zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt in Frankfurt am Main, Freiburg oder remote. Wir sind sehr gespannt, auf deine Bewerbung. Einfach klicken und abschicken!

Deine Aufgaben

  • Du organisierst das perfekte Onboarding für unsere neuen Kunden und begleitest sie durch den Prozess in unserer Software

  • Du betreust unsere Kunden aus dem Bereich der kaufmännischen Betriebsführung für Wind- und Solarparks und hast hierbei keine Berührungsängste mit rechtlich-regulatorischen Themen

  • Du erklärst Kunden, wie sie opti.node optimal nutzen können und hörst dabei genau hin, um weitere Anforderungen und Wünsche zu erkennen

  • Du hältst auch nach dem erfolgreichen Onboarding regelmäßig Kontakt zu Kunden, um neue Funktionen in opti.node zu erläutern und weitere Anknüpfungspunkte zur Zusammenarbeit zu besprechen

  • Du bist das Gesicht zu unseren Kunden, kennst und löst ihre individuellen Herausforderungen und führst sie so zum Erfolg

  • Du arbeitest eng mit dem Produktmanagement, den Product Ownern und dem Sales-Team zusammen, um Anforderungen von Kunden zu bewerten und neue Funktionen zu spezifizieren

Was Du mitbringen solltest

  • Du bringst einen energiewirtschaftlichen Studienhintergrund oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung mit und hast Kenntnisse in mindestens einem der folgenden Themenfelder:

  1. Erfahrung in Direktvermarktung, Energiehandel, Energiedienstleistungen o.ä.

  2. Energiewirtschaftliche Abgaben & Privilegierungen oder Meldepflichten

  3. Kenntnisse in energiewirtschaftlichen Prozessen und Abläufen zwischen verschiedenen Marktakteuren wie Netzbetreibern, Messstellenbetreibern, Lieferanten etc.

  • Du hast bereits Erfahrung im Customer Success gesammelt, hast Freude an der Interaktion mit B2B-Kunden und kannst Dich in andere hineinversetzen

  • Du hast Freude am Lösen komplexer Aufgaben, arbeitest Dich gerne tief ein und willst (technische) Prozesse verstehen und hinterfragen

  • Du arbeitest gerne mit digitalen Tools (Hubspot, Confluence, Miro, Teams und unserer eigenen Software) und bist für Excel immer zu haben

  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf C2 Niveau (unsere Unternehmenssprache) und besitzt gute Englischkenntnisse

Was Du sonst noch bekommst

  • Job mit Sinn: Wir treiben gemeinsam die grüne Energiewende voran

  • Nachhaltige und flexible Arbeitsbedingungen: Unbefristeter Arbeitsertrag, ein ordentliches Gehalt, 30 Tage Urlaub pro Jahr, Remote-First-Kultur mit Büros in Frankfurt a. M. und Freiburg - von wo aus du arbeitest, entscheidest du

  • Strukturierte Einarbeitung: Du bekommst eine strukturierte Einarbeitung, begleitet durch eine:n Mentor:in und eine:n Kolleg:in als Social Buddy für deine soziale Integration bei node.energy

  • Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten: Du wirkst aktiv an der stetigen Entwicklung unseres Unternehmens mit und das ohne starre Prozesse, hierarchische Strukturen oder veraltete Technologien

  • Weiterbildung: Jährliches Weiterbildungsbudget und regelmäßige Feedbackgespräche zur Förderung deiner individuellen Entwicklung

  • Persönliche Treffen: Monatliche Teamtage und jährige Teamevents vor Ort zur persönlichen Zusammenarbeit und Vernetzung - diese sind aber freiwillig

  • Workation: Nach der Probezeit hast du die Möglichkeit, im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Bestimmungen temporär an einem Ort innerhalb der EU zu arbeiten

  • Eine Vielzahl weiterer Benefits: Bahncard, Bezuschussung des Job-Tickets, Bikeleasing, Urban Sports Club/Hansefit, nilo.health Zugang und betriebliche Altersvorsorge

data.title: Activation and Production Testing Specialist
data.description:
🌍 About Hopae

At Hopae, we're building the world's most trusted digital identity platform — private, secure, and built for real life. We believe identity should be in your control — not locked behind outdated systems or centralized gatekeepers.

Our product, Hopae Connect, lets businesses verify real people across borders through a single API — no need to build country-by-country integrations themselves. Our technology powers instant, privacy-first verification across fintech, credentials, supply chain, and gaming — for IDV providers, e-signature platforms, and enterprises who need identity to just work, everywhere.

Backed by top global investors, Hopae operates across Seoul, Paris, Luxembourg, and San Francisco, bringing together exceptional talent from over 10 nationalities. We move fast, think globally, and build products that define the future of identity.

💡 Why You’ll Love It Here

  • Global DNA: Work with exceptional peers across Seoul, Paris, and San Francisco

  • High Impact: Build technology shaping the global trust and identity landscape

  • Ownership Culture: No micromanagement — full trust, full accountability

  • Elite Standards: Work fast, learn fast, and grow with world-class peers

  • Inclusive & Respectful: 10+ nationalities, diverse perspectives, one vision

  • Growth Mindset: Access mentorship, leadership visibility, and continuous learning

What You Will Do

A signed contract is the start of a customer’s journey, not the finish line. On our Activation & Assurance team, you’ll help customers complete provider onboarding, understand how our product works, and validate their integration with real production testers.

This is a junior, hands-on role for someone who enjoys organized work, clear communication, and getting the details right. You’ll start with established playbooks and test procedures, then help improve them as you learn the product and settle into the team.

  • Run activation workflows. Follow provider-specific manuals to submit onboarding requests and coordinate registrations, approvals, and contracting steps with identity providers. Receive credentials and enter them accurately into the Hopae Console, following security procedures and checking the customer and environment.

  • Provide eID-specific activation guidance. When customer involvement is needed, explain the provider’s activation requirements, collect the necessary information, and guide customers through the steps they need to complete.

  • Recruit and manage production testers. Find and onboard testers for the countries and identity providers involved, confirm their eligibility and availability, explain what they need to do, and maintain an organized, reliable tester network.

  • Coordinate and run real-world tests. Once a customer has integrated our product, organize testing with real production testers. Agree on schedules, prepare test scenarios and instructions, guide testers through the user journey, and keep testing on track. Support recurring production checks using the team’s established procedures.

  • Collect evidence and report results. Gather tester feedback and supporting evidence, check outcomes against the expected user flow, and produce clear reports showing what was tested, what worked, what failed, and what still needs attention.

  • Raise issues and follow through. Turn test findings into actionable issues with reproduction steps and relevant evidence. Coordinate with Engineering, Product, and provider-facing teams, track progress, and arrange retesting when fixes are ready. You don’t need to fix the underlying code yourself, but you do need to keep the follow-up moving.

  • Keep people and information aligned. Maintain accurate records of activation status, test coverage, schedules, and blockers. Keep customers, testers, and internal teams informed, and flag missing information or schedule risks early.

  • Help improve how we work. As you gain experience, identify recurring friction and improve checklists, documentation, and handoffs. You’ll also help monitor existing operational automations, check their outputs, and flag exceptions or improvement opportunities.

Who You Are

  • You are detail-driven and dependable. You can follow defined processes consistently, check information carefully, and complete repeatable work without losing accuracy or leaving loose ends.

  • You work in an organized way. You can manage multiple requests and test schedules, keep records current, and follow up with the right people to meet agreed timelines.

  • You communicate clearly and patiently. You’re comfortable working with customers, external testers, and identity providers. You can explain instructions, ask useful questions, and keep people informed without overwhelming them.

  • You are good at gathering and structuring information. You can turn scattered feedback, screenshots, and observations into a clear test report or issue that someone else can act on. You distinguish confirmed findings from things that still need investigation.

  • You have practical technical curiosity. You can learn your way around APIs, credentials, configuration settings, and test versus production environments. You don’t need to be a developer or an identity expert, but you should be comfortable reading documentation and following technical instructions.

  • You know when to ask for help. You recognize when something falls outside the playbook, escalate with useful context, and handle credentials and tester information carefully.

  • You want to grow beyond the checklist. You’re happy to learn established workflows first, then use what you’ve learned to suggest practical process improvements. We don’t expect you to arrive with every answer.

  • You work comfortably in Korean and English. You can communicate with local teammates and international customers, testers, and providers, both in writing and in conversation.

  • Bonus: Experience in customer onboarding, operations, testing coordination, technical support, or customer success. Familiarity with B2B SaaS or digital identity is helpful, but not required.

⚡️ Fast Facts

  • 💰 $13.5M+ raised from top global investors

  • 📦 2.6M+ downloads of our sd-jwt-js library

  • 🌍 10+ nationalities across 3 hubs

  • 🔬 82 eID research projects completed

  • 🌐 3 projects accepted into the OpenWallet Foundation

🎁 Benefits & Culture

  • Unlimited PTO

  • Remote-friendly work model

  • Real ownership from Day 1

  • High-impact, global product

  • Multicultural, respectful team

🧭 Interview Process

  1. Recruiter Intro Call (30 min) – Get to know Hopae

  2. Functional or Technical Interview (45 min) – Dive into your skills

  3. Culture Fit Conversation (45 min) – Collaboration & alignment

  4. Offer 🎉

Note: The process may vary slightly depending on the role.
